overview: This bill makes permanent a $5,000 fee that federal courts must charge people convicted of certain serious crimes, including human trafficking, child sexual exploitation, sexual abuse, and human smuggling. The fee, called a special assessment, is added on top of the standard court assessment and applies only to people or entities who are not too poor to pay. Under current law the requirement has an end date; the bill removes that time limit so the assessment continues indefinitely. The money collected supports a federal fund for trafficking victims. The Senate passed it on December 10, 2025, and as of December 11, 2025, it was awaiting action in the House.
for: Supporters say making the fee permanent ensures that people convicted of trafficking and abuse crimes keep paying toward services for victims, without Congress having to renew it again and again.
against: Critics say a permanent mandatory fee removes the regular chance for Congress to review whether it works as intended, and stacking financial penalties on people leaving prison can make it harder for them to rebuild their lives.
